**RA Progress Statement — Seoul–Daegu Honorific Shift Corpus**
Reporting date: Monday, November 9, 2026
Prepared by: [Your name], Research Assistant, Linguistics PhD Program
Advisor: Prof. Hollander
Funding source: NSF, [grant number]
Submitted for: Winter 2027 funding review

**Status.** 4,200 of the 6,000 utterances targeted for the fall term are complete (70%), all on the Seoul–Daegu honorific shift corpus, which I am the only RA annotating. I expect to reach the full 6,000 by the end of January 2027 at my current rate.

**Cause of the schedule variance.** The remaining 1,800 utterances reflect a six-week hold on data access, not annotation pace. I submitted an IRB amendment on September 3, 2026 to add the 14 new Daegu recordings. Prof. Hollander signed it on October 15, 2026, and annotation on those recordings could not begin before that date. I sent follow-up reminders on September 12, September 24, and October 6; the emails documenting the submission, the reminders, and the signature are in the project thread and are available on request. September 3 to October 15 is exactly six weeks — the same six weeks described in the November 6 lab meeting.

**Work completed during that period.** While the amendment was pending, I continued productive work on the project: at Prof. Hollander's August request, I recoded the existing 2,300 utterances using the revised speech-level scheme. This recoding was not part of the original timeline or the 6,000-utterance target, and each item had to be re-adjudicated against the new categories. These 2,300 recoded utterances are included in the 4,200 total.

**Annotation rate.** Since October 15, I have completed approximately 1,900 utterances — an average of more than 500 per week against a planned rate of 350. The schedule variance is therefore attributable to the signature period and not to throughput.

**Requested entry in the review record.** I ask that the review note record the September 3–October 15 IRB signature period as the cause of the schedule variance, and that the recoding of 2,300 utterances under the revised scheme be counted as term progress. If the November 6 remark that the project is "six weeks behind" is retained in the file, I ask that it be accompanied by this statement and the dates above.
